ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Consider the L-shaped tromino below with 3 attached unit squares. It is cut into exactly two pieces of equal area by a line segment whose endpoints lie on the perimeter of the tromino. What is the longest possible length of the line segment? <image1>
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: What is shown in the image is an L-shaped triomino composed of 3 connected unit squares; these small figures are only rotations or reflections of the same L-shaped triomino. Therefore one may choose any orientation for modeling. Take this L shape as a 2×2 square with the upper-right 1×1 square removed, with coordinate vertices in order (0,0),(2,0),(2,1),(1,1),(1,2),(0,2). The total area is 3, so when it is cut into two pieces of equal area, each piece has area 3/2. According to the method draft, enumerate the edges on which the endpoints lie. If the endpoints are on the left outer edge and the bottom outer edge, let them be respectively (0,t) and (s,0), where 0<s,t≤2. This line segment cuts off a right triangle near the origin, with area st/2. The equal-area condition gives st/2=3/2, that is, st=3. The length of the line segment is sqrt(s^2+t^2). From t=3/s and 0<s,t≤2, one obtains s∈[3/2,2]. Thus the square of the length is s^2+9/s^2, and its maximum is attained at the endpoints of the interval: when (s,t)=(2,3/2) or (3/2,2), the square of the length is 4+9/4=25/4, so the length is 5/2. Comparing the remaining edge pairs: if the endpoints are near adjacent small edges or the reentrant edge, the horizontal or vertical span is at most 1 or the area cannot reach 3/2, so the length does not exceed sqrt(5)<5/2, or an equal-area cut cannot be formed. If the endpoints are on the upper and lower outer edges or the left and right outer edges, the equal-area condition reduces to a linear condition similar to a+s=3/2, and the maximum is also reached only when the endpoint degenerates to the above left-edge/bottom-edge case, reaching 5/2. If the endpoints are on the top outer edge and the right outer edge, except for the special case passing through the diagonal from (0,2) to (2,0), the line segment will pass through the missing unit square; although this special diagonal is longer, the areas it separates are 2 and 1, not equal areas. Therefore, among all feasible equal-area cuts, the longest length is 5/2.

method.method_draft: First read the image as an L-tromino made of three unit squares, congruent to a 2 by 2 square with one unit corner square removed; choose one orientation since the displayed orientations are rotations/reflections. Put coordinates on the L as the polygon with vertices (0,0), (2,0), (2,1), (1,1), (1,2), (0,2). From the text, the cutting segment has endpoints on the perimeter and must split total area 3 into two areas of 3/2. Enumerate possible pairs of boundary edges for the two endpoints, discard segments that pass through the missing unit square, and for each remaining case compute the area on one side by shoelace or elementary triangle/trapezoid formulas. In the maximizing case the endpoints lie on two perpendicular outer sides, say (0,t) and (s,0), cutting off a right triangle of area st/2. The equal-area condition gives st/2 = 3/2, so st = 3, with 0 < s,t <= 2 from the 2 by 2 bounding box. Compare lengths sqrt(s^2+t^2) over the feasible interval; the maximum is at (s,t) = (2,3/2) or (3/2,2), giving length sqrt(4 + 9/4) = 5/2. The edge-pair enumeration verifies that all other perimeter-pair cases are no longer.

按方法草案枚举端点所在的边。若端点在左外边和下外边，设它们分别为 (0,t) 与 (s,0)，其中 0<s,t≤2。该线段切下靠近原点的直角三角形，面积为 st/2。等面积条件给出 st/2=3/2，即 st=3。线段长度为 sqrt(s^2+t^2)。由 t=3/s 且 0<s,t≤2，可得 s∈[3/2,2]。于是长度平方为 s^2+9/s^2，其最大值在区间端点取得：当 (s,t)=(2,3/2) 或 (3/2,2) 时，长度平方为 4+9/4=25/4，所以长度为 5/2。

其余边对比较：若端点在相邻的小边或内凹边附近，横向或纵向跨度至多为 1 或面积无法达到 3/2，因此长度不超过 sqrt(5)<5/2，或不能形成等面积切割。若端点在上下外边或左右外边，等面积条件化为类似 a+s=3/2 的线性条件，最大也只在端点退化到上述左边/下边情形时达到 5/2。若端点在上外边和右外边，除经过对角线 (0,2) 到 (2,0) 的特殊情况外线段会穿过缺失的单位方格；该特殊对角线虽然更长，但分出的面积为 2 和 1，不是等面积。因此所有可行等面积切割中最长长度为 5/2。

method.method_draft: First describe the figure as a three-unit-square L inside a 2 by 2 square with one missing corner square. Use the text to note that each side of the cut must have area 3/2. Instead of enumerating every edge pair, argue geometrically that a longest equal-area chord must span two full outer sides of the enclosing 2 by 2 square; chords ending on the concave notch or on the short exterior arms have a smaller available horizontal/vertical span and can be bounded below the eventual candidate. Thus reduce the extremal cut to the hypotenuse of a right triangle cut from one outer corner of the tromino. Let the intercept lengths along the two perpendicular outer sides be a and b. The triangle lies inside the L, has area ab/2, and must equal 3/2, so ab = 3. Since the figure’s bounding dimensions are 2 by 2, both intercepts satisfy a,b <= 2, hence the feasible product-3 pairs lie between 3/2 and 2. The cut length is sqrt(a^2+b^2); with fixed product 3 and upper bounds 2, this is maximized at the most unequal feasible pair, namely {a,b} = {2,3/2}. Therefore the longest segment has length sqrt(2^2 + (3/2)^2) = 5/2.

raw_record.original_question:
Consider the L-shaped tromino below with 3 attached unit squares. It is cut into exactly two pieces of equal area by a line segment whose endpoints lie on the perimeter of the tromino. What is the longest possible length of the line segment?
<image1>
raw_record.final_cot:
What is shown in the image is an L-shaped triomino composed of 3 connected unit squares; these small figures are only rotations or reflections of the same L-shaped triomino. Therefore one may choose any orientation for modeling. Take this L shape as a 2×2 square with the upper-right 1×1 square removed, with coordinate vertices in order (0,0),(2,0),(2,1),(1,1),(1,2),(0,2). The total area is 3, so when it is cut into two pieces of equal area, each piece has area 3/2.

According to the method draft, enumerate the edges on which the endpoints lie. If the endpoints are on the left outer edge and the bottom outer edge, let them be respectively (0,t) and (s,0), where 0<s,t≤2. This line segment cuts off a right triangle near the origin, with area st/2. The equal-area condition gives st/2=3/2, that is, st=3. The length of the line segment is sqrt(s^2+t^2). From t=3/s and 0<s,t≤2, one obtains s∈[3/2,2]. Thus the square of the length is s^2+9/s^2, and its maximum is attained at the endpoints of the interval: when (s,t)=(2,3/2) or (3/2,2), the square of the length is 4+9/4=25/4, so the length is 5/2.

Comparing the remaining edge pairs: if the endpoints are near adjacent small edges or the reentrant edge, the horizontal or vertical span is at most 1 or the area cannot reach 3/2, so the length does not exceed sqrt(5)<5/2, or an equal-area cut cannot be formed. If the endpoints are on the upper and lower outer edges or the left and right outer edges, the equal-area condition reduces to a linear condition similar to a+s=3/2, and the maximum is also reached only when the endpoint degenerates to the above left-edge/bottom-edge case, reaching 5/2. If the endpoints are on the top outer edge and the right outer edge, except for the special case passing through the diagonal from (0,2) to (2,0), the line segment will pass through the missing unit square; although this special diagonal is longer, the areas it separates are 2 and 1, not equal areas. Therefore, among all feasible equal-area cuts, the longest length is 5/2.
